evals.expected_output: An executable spec file with testable acceptance criteria, repo-derived assumptions with evidence, and at most 5 ranked open questions.
expectations: A spec file is written containing goal, non-goals, acceptance criteria, assumptions, and open questions
Every acceptance criterion names a concrete check (test, command, or manual step) — none is a vague 'works correctly'
Repository investigation happens before user questions, and investigation-resolved decisions carry file:line evidence
Open questions number 5 or fewer and are ranked by architectural impact
The chat response leads with a short summary, not the full spec body

evals.prompt: Turn this into a proper spec: 'make the game feel less grindy in the mid-game, obviously without breaking existing saves'.
evals.expected_output: The throwaway save-compatibility clause is captured as a requirement; ambiguous phrases quoted verbatim.
expectations: Save compatibility appears as an explicit requirement or acceptance criterion
The ambiguous phrase 'less grindy' is quoted and operationalized into measurable criteria or a ranked question
Every user-stated requirement appears in exactly one of criteria, non-goals, or open questions

evals.prompt: Write acceptance criteria for the new pet-breeding feature before we build it.
evals.expected_output: Spec triggered by explicit request; criteria grounded in the existing pet catalog conventions.
expectations: Existing repository conventions (e.g. config catalog shape) are cited as the basis for interface decisions
Defaults chosen on the user's behalf are labeled as reversible assumptions

evals.prompt: Spec out the thing we discussed.
evals.expected_output: Adversarial: no goal is derivable; the skill asks the top ranked questions instead of writing fiction.
expectations: No invented spec is produced from thin air
The response asks at most 3 targeted questions to establish the goal
